predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Praetorian prefecture of Italy'. The Exarchate is the Eastern Roman Empire's own province (Cliopatria has no row for it), so the hand-over is administrative; the land is what the Lombard invasion of 568 left of the prefecture re-won from the Ostrogoths in 540-554.

successors.note: 751-756; the Lombards are a Cliopatria row (Lombards 569-586 shape for Italy, then inside Kingdom of Italy 587..1946, which data/README.md lists as wrong). Another group should say which dossier carries the Lombard kingdom after 586.

region.text: Ravenna 'with its port and environs, north to the Po and south to the Marecchia', the Pentapolis, and 'a group of duchies including Rome, Venetia, Calabria, Naples, Perugia, and Lucania', 'mainly the coastal cities'; Istria and Liguria are the page's other holdings. Lombard land lay between them, so the rendering agent should draw this union only where no Lombard shape is drawn.

ledger.note: 584: the Byzantines set up an exarch at Ravenna. 'The exarchate was established around 584, the year in which the presence of an exarch in Ravenna is attested for the first time'; infobox 'Foundation of Exarchate: 584'. The first exarch is Decius (584-585). The page names the cities and duchies, not a boundary, and says 'mainly the coastal cities'.

region.text: Liguria, 'completely lost in 640 to the Lombards'

ledger.note: 640: Liguria falls to the Lombards. 'completely lost in 640 to the Lombards' (Exarchate page). The Rothari page says 'Rothari conquered Genoa in 641' and takes the remaining Eastern Roman Liguria 'around 643'; the Exarchate page's 640 is used.

region.text: the remaining Eastern Roman territories in the lower Po valley, including Oderzo

ledger.note: 641: Rothari takes the last imperial land of the Veneto mainland. The page: Rothari took 'the remaining Eastern Roman territories in the lower Po valley, including Oderzo, in 641'; it adds that he 'recaptured Oderzo at same year' (the sentence is garbled; 645, the year of Plato's defeat on the Scultenna, is the page's other date). The lagoon around Venice stays imperial.

region.text: Bologna, Osimo, Ancona, Rimini, the Pentapolis, the cities of Emilia and Classe, taken in Liutprand's 727 campaign

ledger.note: 727: Liutprand overruns the Exarchate's march. The page dates Bologna, Osimo, Ancona, Rimini, the Pentapolis ('spontaneously' submitting) and Classe to the 727 campaign; 'he could not take Ravenna itself'. Context on the Exarchate page: the exarch's seat 'until the revolt of 727 over iconoclasm'.

region.text: Sutri, seized in 727 and 'handed to papacy' in 728 (the Donation of Sutri)

ledger.note: 728: Liutprand gives Sutri to the papacy. The page: 'Seized 727 / handed to papacy 728' after the pope's payments, the Donation of Sutri; month silent. Sutri lay in the Duchy of Rome, which the 584 shape counts as Exarchate land.

region.text: the Pentapolis and the Ravenna march, listed as Exarchate territory in 740

ledger.note: 740: the Pentapolis is again listed with the Exarchate. Bridging: the Exarchate page lists 'Istria, Venetia, Ferrara, Ravenna... with the Pentapolis, and Perugia' as the remaining territory in 740; the Liutprand page says the Venetian-aligned Duke Ursus and Patriarch Antoninus expelled the Lombards from Ravenna after 731 but gives no date for the Pentapolis. A gap-filler should open the Venice or Liutprand-era sources.

region.text: Rome and its duchy, where the pope was 'the real master'

ledger.note: 740: Rome drops out of the Exarchate's list. Bridging: the page names Rome among the late 6th-century duchies, says the pope 'was the real master' there, and omits it from the 740 list of remaining territory; it gives no year for the separation.

region.text: Naples, Calabria and Lucania, 'overrun by Benevento' (Calabria, Naples)

ledger.note: 740: the south is gone. Bridging: the page says Naples and Calabria were 'overrun by Benevento' and leaves them out of the 740 list; it gives no year, and Naples had its own dukes (Cliopatria's Duchy of Naples begins 763).

region.text: Ravenna and 'all the provinces subject to the Exarchate'

ledger.note: 751: Aistulf takes Ravenna. 'The exarchate fell in 751 with the Lombard conquest of Ravenna at the hands of the Lombard king Aistulf' and the exarch Eutychius was killed; month silent. The Aistulf page dates the capture of 'Ravenna and all the provinces subject to the Exarchate' to 750. The Exarchate page puts the Ducatus Pentapolis in 752; it is folded in here so the shape ends with the state.

region.text: 'Istria, Venetia, Ferrara, Ravenna... with the Pentapolis, and Perugia': the page's list of the remaining territory at 740

ledger.note: 751: the Exarchate of Ravenna falls. The Lombards hold its land until the Franks make Aistulf return it in 755-756 ('Pepin promised to restore the exarchate of Ravenna' in 754 and the 756 treaty gave its territories to the pope, per the Donation of Pepin page). Venice is the page's third successor.

wars.name: Lombard invasion of Italy
wars.outcome: The Lombards under Alboin took Milan (569) and Pavia (572, after a three-year siege), split into duchies after Alboin's murder (573), and killed the imperial general Baduarius in 576; Tiberius II reorganised what was left into five provinces in 580 and the exarchate emerged around 584.
wars.note: Cliopatria's Lombards shape for 569-586 covers the north; the Exarchate dossier's keyframe begins at the end of this war, so no zone is drawn.

wars.name: Rothari's conquest of Liguria and the lower Po
wars.outcome: Rothari took the Ligurian coast, 'all the cities of the Romans' from Luna westward, and the remaining imperial land of the lower Po valley including Oderzo in 641; the exarch Plato's counter-invasion was beaten on the Scultenna near Modena in 645 with the loss of 8,000 men.
wars.note: Paul the Deacon's wording is quoted on the page for Luni; the year for Luni is not given.

wars.name: Liutprand's war with the Exarchate

zones.text: Bologna, the Pentapolis, Emilia and Classe, 727

wars.outcome: Liutprand took Bologna, Osimo, Ancona, Rimini, the Pentapolis, Emilia and Classe in 727 but not Ravenna; Sutri went to the pope in 728; Venetians expelled the Lombards from Ravenna after 731; by 740 the Pentapolis is listed with the Exarchate again.
wars.note: The war's end year is the Exarchate page's 740 list, not a treaty date.

wars.name: Aistulf's conquest of Ravenna and the Frankish intervention
wars.outcome: Aistulf took Ravenna (751; 750 on the Aistulf page) and the Pentapolis (752); Pepin forced him to return Roman lands in 755 and again in 756, after Aistulf's second siege of Rome, and the 756 treaty gave the Exarchate's territories to the pope.
wars.note: Pepin promised 'to restore the exarchate of Ravenna' at Ponthion on 6 January 754 (Donation of Pepin page); the Empire's envoys offered a large sum and were refused. The treaty text has not survived.

certainty.note: The Exarchate was a string of coastal cities and corridors between Lombard lands; no treaty line survives. The Ravenna-Pentapolis march is the best known; the Perugia corridor and the Venetian and Istrian holdings are approximate.

notes: Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free. Five pages opened; the page budget was spent. Not settled: (1) the page gives no area; (2) Rome, Naples, Calabria and Lucania leave the Exarchate in the unnamed years before the page's 740 list (ledger confidence 1); Naples's own duchy is eu-13's; (3) the recovery of the Pentapolis between 727 and 740 and Venice's separation (697 or 705 in other sources) are not on the pages opened; (4) the Exarchate page gives 751 and the Aistulf page 750 for the fall of Ravenna; the Pentapolis is 752 on the Exarchate page; (5) the Lombards' Italian kingdom needs its own dossier after 586 (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy 587..1946 is a known-bad row). Sutri is not in the gazetteer (listed in the report). Catepanate of Italy (975-1071) is a later successor in Apulia and is a separate state.
